blocks.text: Condo buildings in Sardis South

Its headline finding is a tenure finding: the verified freehold apartment-condo count for Sardis South is ZERO. The area's two named apartment buildings — Skynest (Watson Road) and The Yearling (Chilliwack River Road) — are both First Nations leasehold, and its other apartment product is purpose-built rental or manufactured-home park stock; all are documented below as excluded, with reasons.
Streets, schools and getting around Sardis South

items.t: "Sardis South" is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack; the City publishes no boundary for it.

Plan frame: Sardis South sits inside the Schedule B5 Sardis Neighbourhood Plan area of the 2050 OCP (Bylaw 2025, No. 5500); the Agricultural Plan is Schedule B1 of the same bylaw and Schedule D is the Development Permit Areas schedule.

Where the apartment stock actually sits: two leasehold buildings — Skynest at the Watson Road / Vedder Road corner (45745 and 45757 Watson Road) and The Yearling in the Iron Horse community (6045 Chilliwack River Road) — plus a purpose-built rental building on Vedder Road (McGill Apartments).

blocks.text: Good to know about Sardis South

items.t: Sardis South's "condo market" is a leasehold market. Both of its modern apartment buildings stand on Tzeachten First Nations land (Skynest at Watson/Vedder, The Yearling at Iron Horse) — the buildings are new (2022–2024), the amenities are real, and the tenure is leasehold in both cases, so every freehold assumption (Form B, depreciation report, PTT/GST treatment, lender terms) has to be re-derived from the lease documents.

The Yearling is marketed two ways at once. The developer sells its 86 condos as ownership product while a rental platform markets units in the same building to tenants, noting the Residential Tenancy Act does not apply on Tzeachten land — an investor reading only the sales material will miss the tenancy frame entirely.
A 45+ label here is not a strata bylaw. Skynest's 45+ and Promontory Lake Estates' 45+ positions live in lease/park documents, where BC's strata rule (only 55+ is lawful, SPA ss.
Flood diligence is a Vedder-side question, not a page claim.

The Sardis Sports Complex / Sardis Library pair anchors this sub-area, not Sardis West Vedder. Both facilities (5725 and 5819 Tyson Road) are in Sardis South, a placement the neighbouring guide page itself records — "walk to the rink/library" claims for west-side product should be measured, not assumed.

blocks.text: Sardis South: streets and boundaries

items.t: Sardis South has no City-published boundary; it is the southern part of Sardis in the City of Chilliwack, around Tyson Road, South Sumas Road and Watson Road, roughly south of Stevenson Road.
The whole of Sardis, including Sardis South, sits inside Schedule B5 (Sardis) of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500.
Sardis South is a Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (CADREB) market name, not a Fraser Valley board sub-area, and CADREB publishes statistics board-wide only.
Vedder Road is the eastern edge: Sardis East Vedder and Promontory lie east of it, Sardis West Vedder west of it, and Vedder Crossing and Garrison Crossing lie to the south toward the Vedder River.

blocks.text: Sardis South: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) allows 3 to 4 units on eligible single-detached and duplex zoned lots over 280 square metres inside the urban growth boundary, under Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395.
New secondary suites are not permitted below the flood construction level, which limits basement suites on the Vedder River side of Sardis South.
Short-term rentals are a regulated use under Short-Term Rental Bylaw 2021, No. 5141, not an as-of-right use of a house.

blocks.text: Sardis South: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Route 58 Tyson is the Sardis South bus: a loop from Cottonwood Mall via Tyson Road at Keith Wilson Road and Tyson Road at Watson Road, running roughly hourly on weekdays.
Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road, is a Fraser Valley Regional Library branch, not a City library.
Sardis Sports Complex is at 5725 Tyson Road, on the City's facility list, a short walk from Mount Slesse Middle School at 5871 Tyson Road.
SD33 is consulting on balancing enrolment because the district is at 103 percent of functional capacity, so Sardis-area catchment boundaries may change for September 2027 — check current.
The Vedder River dike and the river's alluvial fan sit south of the neighbourhood; flood construction levels are lot-specific, not street-specific.

blocks.text: Sardis South: development and new projects

items.t: Sardis Secondary expansion, 45460 Stevenson Road: a $40-million expansion adding 400 student seats, bringing capacity to 1,600, with a gymnasium refurbishment. STATUS: reported as a School District No. 33 capital project on the project tracker read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: Sardis South: getting around

items.t: BC Transit runs Chilliwack transit, not TransLink; Route 58 Tyson loops through Sardis South from Cottonwood Mall via Tyson Road.
Route 51 Vedder runs the Vedder Road corridor at the east edge of Sardis South, between the University of the Fraser Valley Chilliwack campus and Downtown Chilliwack.
Route 54 Promontory crosses the Stevenson Road side via Wiltshire Street at Stevenson Road and Promontory Road at Vedder Road.
Route 66 Fraser Valley Express, the regional link to Lougheed Town Centre Station, stops at Vedder Road at Luckakuck Way, north of Sardis South.

blocks.text: Sardis South: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the lot against the City's floodplain maps under Floodplain Regulation Bylaw No. 4519 before subjects: the bylaw sets a 75-metre setback from the Vedder River's natural boundary and flood construction levels vary by area.
Lots near creeks fall under Development Permit Area 3, which protects riparian areas and fish habitat; a development permit can be required before building.
